messages:
natasha: heads-up — after yesterday's svc-principal rotate we started seeing Key Vault unwrap failures from prod-service. errors are 'Unauthorized' and sometimes 'Key not found'. no obvious errors in app logs.

sam: are you on RBAC or access policies on the vault?

natasha: RBAC (switched 2 weeks ago). we removed legacy access policies.

sam: ok — couple quick checks: 1) make sure the principal actually has the appropriate data-plane role (RBAC) on the vault (not just mgmt plane). 2) check diagnostic logs for the vault (activity logs won't show key unwraps).

priya: adding details — Key Vault data-plane operations (wrap/unwrap/sign/verify) are emitted to the diagnostic settings (AzureDiagnostics / AuditEvent). if diagnostic settings aren't configured you'll see nothing.

priya: example to enable diag ->
```bash
az monitor diagnostic-settings create --resource "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-prod/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/prod-kv" --name kv-audit --workspace "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-ops/providers/Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/la-prod" --logs '[{"category":"AuditEvent","enabled":true}]'
```

sam: role assignment example (data plane RBAC role):
```bash
az role assignment create --assignee <principal-id> --role "Key Vault Crypto User" --scope /subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-prod/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/prod-kv
```

mike: note on managed identities vs service principals: user-assigned and system-assigned managed identities are tenant-bound. if the workload is running under a principal from a different tenant, RBAC won't work unless that identity exists as a guest/service principal in the vault's tenant.

natasha: hmm — our prod-service runs in a different subscription that used to be in the same tenant but was moved. could that explain it?

priya: yep. common pitfall: after tenant/subscription moves the client_id in secrets or kube manifests can still point at the old SP (or a deleted one). diagnostics usually show the client_id that attempted the operation.

sam: other thing — key rotation and envelope encryption: if you rotate the KEK (key version), unwrap behavior can change if callers reference a specific key version. If the app expects the latest key but the DEK was wrapped with an old version, you may need to rewrap DEKs against the current version or ensure the code uses the right key version in unwrap calls.

priya: quick runbook to triage unwrap failures:
- enable diagnostic settings (AuditEvent) -> confirm unwrap/wrap attempts and returned status
- check the caller/principal id in the logs vs expected principal
- verify vault's access model (RBAC vs access policies) and any leftover access policy entries
- inspect key versions: `az keyvault key show --id https://prod-kv.vault.azure.net/keys/my-key`
- if rotation happened, consider rewrapping DEKs or using key-versioned URIs

natasha: enabled diag and pulled logs — shows client_id = xxxxx that doesn't match our new svc-principal. it's the old staging client id. looks like kube secret never updated.

mike: ok that's a config drift then. we should: 1) patch kube to use the new managed identity/SP, 2) ensure principal has the "Key Vault Crypto User" role on the vault, 3) if any DEKs were re-encrypted with a different key version, plan a rewrap.

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-4382 -> "AKV unwrap failures due to cross-tenant principal mismatch". linked runbook: /runbooks/akv-unwrap-triage

priya: for the docs: we should highlight the difference between ActivityLog vs Diagnostic logs and call out that key operations are only in Diagnostic (AuditEvent). also note guest SP patterns for cross-tenant access.

natasha: thanks — I'll update the kube secret and confirm. assigning rewrap/DEK work to mike and docs to priya. :thumbsup:

mike: will rewrap if needed. will coordinate with natasha before doing wide changes.

natasha: resolved — fixed secret, unwraps succeed, diag shows successful unwraps from new principal. will follow up with a short postmortem and update the onboarding doc to include tenant checks. :white_check_mark:
